answer: Bind each agent identity to a single hardware enclave key — one ferrous chip, one persona, so a farm cannot mint a thousand agents from one machine. Trust is not granted at registration: it accrues only from a continuous river of attested useful work, each task adding a small, decaying credit. An idle identity becomes a relic: its credit erodes to zero within a few epochs unless refreshed by new verified work. An attacker must therefore buy a real chip per clone and keep every clone working forever; the fleet plus endless upkeep costs more than any reward the network pays.
